---
title: "Cross-references"
subtitle: "Label a block, caption it, and point at it."
description: "Cross-referencing compiled Typst blocks with label, cap, and alt, for figures, tables, listings, and custom reference types."
# A ```{typst} block looks like an executable cell to Quarto's engine
# detection, which then selects Jupyter and fails for want of a kernel. The
# extension compiles those blocks itself, so the page needs no engine.
engine: markdown
---

A compiled block is a Quarto cross-reference target like any other.
Three options do the work:

- `label` names the block, and its prefix selects the reference type.
- `cap` is the caption below it.
- `alt` is the text for a reader who cannot see the image.

## A figure

````markdown
```{typst}
//| label: fig-shapes
//| cap: "A circle and a square, drawn by Typst."
//| alt: "A blue circle beside an orange square."
#stack(
  dir: ltr,
  spacing: 1em,
  circle(radius: 1cm, fill: blue.lighten(60%)),
  rect(width: 2cm, height: 2cm, fill: orange.lighten(60%)),
)
```

See @fig-shapes.
````

```{typst}
//| label: fig-shapes
//| cap: "A circle and a square, drawn by Typst."
//| alt: "A blue circle beside an orange square."
#stack(
  dir: ltr,
  spacing: 1em,
  circle(radius: 1cm, fill: blue.lighten(60%)),
  rect(width: 2cm, height: 2cm, fill: orange.lighten(60%)),
)
```

See @fig-shapes.

## A table

The prefix of the label decides the type, so a `tbl-` label gives a table, numbered in its own series:

````markdown
```{typst}
//| label: tbl-formats
//| cap: "How each writer receives a block."
//| alt: "A table of three output formats and how each one receives a block."
#table(
  columns: 2,
  [*Writer*], [*Receives*],
  [html], [image],
  [latex], [image],
  [typst], [native or image],
)
```

@tbl-formats lists them.
````

```{typst}
//| label: tbl-formats
//| cap: "How each writer receives a block."
//| alt: "A table of three output formats and how each one receives a block."
#table(
  columns: 2,
  [*Writer*], [*Receives*],
  [html], [image],
  [latex], [image],
  [typst], [native or image],
)
```

@tbl-formats lists them.

Every Quarto prefix works the same way, `lst-` and the custom types a document declares included.

## Prefix-specific captions

`cap` and `alt` apply to any label.
The prefixed forms, `fig-cap`, `tbl-cap`, `lst-cap`, and their `alt` counterparts, say the same thing for one type:

```typ
//| label: fig-example
//| fig-cap: "A caption for a figure."
//| fig-alt: "Alternative text for a figure."
```

A prefixed option takes precedence over the generic one when the label matches its type.
Write `cap` and `alt` unless a document already uses the prefixed names.

::: {.callout-important}
Reference the filter by name, with no `at:` stage.
Pinning it to one stage breaks cross-referencing, because the labels must be in place before Quarto numbers them.
:::
